column1: # super-r1.tsv -- DUMPBIOS, Super (GEMDOS 0x20) and Supexec (XBIOS 0x26): the
# processor-state calls behind the NewTOS super state (TASK/MEM12,
# Form: docs/TOS-REFERENCE-DUMPER.md section 6, "The call table, as built for
# DUMPBIOS" and "Super and Supexec in a BIOS-area table".  f:<n> is the
# 1 returns -2, 2 returns what Super(1L) answers inside the callback.  t:0 is
# the token the last Super(0L) case returned.  Super(0L) ... Super(t:0) is a
# bracket the guard insists on closing; the cases between run in supervisor
# A separate table, so bios-r1.tsv and its references stay as they are.  One
# table per round: the case id is the physical line number and the dump
# header carries the CRC of this file, so it is frozen once measured.

column5: Super(1L) in user state: 0 -- x20_inq, bdos/rwa.S:340-346

column1: # ---- Super(0L): x20_usr, bdos/rwa.S:280-301 -- returns the old SSP (NewTOS: a token, S4)

column5: Super(0L) enters supervisor state, returns the token -- x20_usr, bdos/rwa.S:280-301
Super(1L) in supervisor state: -1 -- x20_inq, bdos/rwa.S:340-346

column1: # ---- SuperToUser: x20_sup, bdos/rwa.S:305-336 -- writes no d0, so IGNORE; the next inquiry measures the state

column5: Super(token) = SuperToUser leaves supervisor state -- x20_sup, bdos/rwa.S:305-336

column1: # ---- Supexec(codeptr): bios/vectors.S:1376-1378, jmp to the callback in supervisor mode

column5: Supexec(cb 2): Super(1L) inside the callback, -1 -- bios/vectors.S:1376-1378, bdos/rwa.S:340-346
Super(1L) after Supexec: 0, the caller's state -- bios/vectors.S:1376-1378
